oil.when: 2015 (reset with the accelerator and brake pedals)
steps: Reset only after the engine oil and filter have actually been changed.
Switch the ignition on without starting the engine.
Press the accelerator and brake pedals down together and keep both fully pressed.
After about three seconds a message says the oil reset is in progress. Keep holding.
After about 25 seconds a message says the reset is complete. Let go of both pedals and switch the ignition off.
oil.note: Checked in the 2015 Transit owner's manual.

tpms.when: 2015, after setting pressures or rotating the tires (front and rear pressures differ)
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressures on the door jamb label. The front and rear numbers are different on this van.
If the tires were rotated, the system has to learn which sensor is now in front and which in back. Start by driving above 20 mph (32 km/h) for at least two minutes.
Park where you can reach all four tires with an air pump, at least three feet from any other Ford doing the same procedure.
Switch the ignition off, then switch it on without starting the engine.
Within 10 seconds, turn the hazard flashers on and off three times. One horn chirp and a flashing tire pressure light mean the system is ready. If not, start again from switching the ignition off.
At the left front tire, take off the valve cap and let air out until the horn chirps once.
Do the same at the right front, then the right rear, then the left rear tire, with no more than two minutes between tires.
A double horn chirp means the procedure timed out or failed: start over from the beginning.
When all four are done, set every tire back to the door jamb pressures.
tpms.note: If the van never gives the single horn chirp after a second try, have a dealer check the system. Checked in the 2015 Transit owner's manual.
